description:
FILED s450u (Opus, round 8 agent U) while closing #477.

#477 removed the QUADRATIC term from a scalar-context `m//g` loop ($&/$`/$'
were built eagerly, copying the whole subject twice per match).  The loop is
now LINEAR, but it is still ~30x slower than perl per match:

    while ($x =~ /./g) { }     (runpcl wall, ~0.20 s of it is startup)
        n         before      after
        1 000      0.18 s     0.23 s
       50 000      1.08 s     0.37 s
      100 000      3.37 s     0.48 s
      200 000     12.80 s     0.72 s
      400 000        --       1.26 s
    1 000 000        --       2.83 s      perl: 0.09 s

So ~2.6 us per match against perl's ~0.09 us.  WHERE IT GOES, not yet
measured with sb-sprof after the fix -- that is the first step, and it is
cheap (the recipe is in #477: profile the qp6 shape, `my $x = "a" x 1000000;
while ($x =~ /./g) { $n++ }`).  The suspects, in order, are all per-match
allocations in the success path of `do-regex-match` -> `set-match-vars`:

  1. @- / @+ are REBUILT per match: two `make-p-box` allocations plus two
     `vector-push-extend` even for a pattern with no capture groups.  perl
     fills those lazily too (they are magic).  The same offsets the #477
     change already stores would serve them.
  2. `clear-capture-groups` writes 20 `$N` specials + two `clrhash` + a
     fill-pointer reset on EVERY successful match, whatever the pattern's
     group count.  A pattern with no groups needs none of it.
  3. `%pcl-create-scanner` is consulted per call -- check that the compiled
     scanner really is cached and that the cache key is not rebuilt from the
     pattern string each time.

Target A (speed must beat perl).  No row count sits behind it today:
t/op/utf8cache.t's "quadratic pos" loop now completes well inside the
companion timeout, which was #477's acceptance.

SHIPPED s454ac (Opus, round 12 perf agent, 2026-08-30; cl/pcl-runtime.lisp
only, no generation bump).

THE PROFILE NAMED A SUSPECT THIS TASK DID NOT LIST, AND IT WAS 66% OF THE
LOOP: the emission calls (p-regex "/./g") inside the loop CONDITION, so the
pattern text was RE-PARSED per iteration -- perl-regex-to-ppcre alone (eight
regex-replace-all passes) was 51% of total, plus parse-regex-modifiers
interning a keyword per modifier char per iteration.  sb-sprof flat on the
qp6 shape at 1M (recipe as filed): p-regex 66.1% total, do-regex-match 27.6%
(of which %pcl-create-scanner's FORMAT-built key 5.8%, set-match-vars 3.4%,
clear-capture-groups 1.9%).  This task's suspect 3 was half right: the
scanner cache itself hits, but the format key was rebuilt per call.

WHAT SHIPPED, in profile order:
 1. p-regex MEMOIZED on its source text (*p-regex-op-cache*, equal hash;
    keys copied via %pcl-memo-key -- a Perl string can be a str-buffer).
    Safe because a match op is immutable after construction and has no
    perl-visible identity.  p-qr is NOT memoized: two qr/a/ evaluations are
    different refaddrs in perl (probed, guard row).
 2. The compiled form CACHED IN THE STRUCT (%compiled slot, lazily filled by
    %p-regex-compiled): #(scanner reg-names closers anchored-g global-p
    cont-p).  Kills the per-match \G strip, build-ppcre-options, the format
    key, and the two modifier getfs.
 3. p-regex-from-parts memoized BOTH ways: the string-pattern branch through
    the same table (key = (mods pattern) LIST, which equal can never
    conflate with p-regex's string keys), and the qr-with-op-flags branch
    through a per-qr %op-variants alist keyed by the modifier string --
    `while ($t =~ /$re/g)` built a fresh derived struct per iteration,
    defeating every downstream cache.
 4. clear-capture-groups HIGH-WATER MARKED (*p-captures-set*, written by
    set-capture-groups): only the $N actually set by the last group-y match
    are re-cleared, so a 0-group loop pays zero of the 20 writes.  PROBED
    FIRST (perl 5.40): a 0-group SUCCESSFUL match DOES clear $1 (suspect
    2's "gate on the pattern's group count" would have been a silent
    wrong); a FAILED match keeps it; a fewer-group match clears the excess.
    All rows identical PCL vs perl before and after.  The one spelling
    outside the invariant is `local $1` restore -- inside #684's known
    block-scoping divergence.  clrhash %+/%- (4 sites) gated on
    hash-table-count > 0.
 5. @-/@+ ELEMENT BOXES REUSED IN PLACE (%p-at-elem-set) instead of
    fill-pointer-reset + 2 fresh make-p-box per match.  This is suspect 1,
    and the probe made it a CORRECTNESS fix too: perl's @-/@+ elements are
    magic, so a saved \$-[0] reads the CURRENT match -- PCL's fresh boxes
    left the ref on the stale box (probed divergence, now identical).
    @-/@+ are read-only in perl, so no program-held box arrives with other
    state.  The full-lazy design this task sketched was REJECTED: a
    materialize-on-read array diverges through a saved \@- (the ref holds
    the materialization from ITS read; perl and today's PCL both show the
    current match) -- box reuse gets the allocation win with array identity
    preserved.
 6. cl-ppcre:scan BYPASSED for the compiled-scanner calls (%p-ppcre-scan =
    direct funcall; ppcre's (scanner function) method is exactly funcall +
    maybe-coerce-to-simple-string + a nil *real-start-pos* rebind, read from
    the installed api.lisp).  Kills the CLOS emf + check-applicable-keywords
    + &rest consing (~7%).  The simple-string coercion HOISTED to once per
    do-regex-match call: ppcre coerced per SCAN, so a non-simple subject (a
    str-buffer) was copied whole per /g step; the hoist also pins
    *match-subject* to a copy no str-buffer append can mutate under a
    deferred $&/$`/$' cut.

MEASURED (runpcl wall, ~0.2s startup; same n-ladder as filed):
    n           before(s450u)  after
    1 000        0.23           0.20
    50 000       0.37           0.20
    100 000      0.48           0.22
    200 000      0.72           0.23
    400 000      1.26           0.27
    1 000 000    2.83           0.40     perl: 0.09
Per-match ~2.6 us -> ~0.21 us (perl 0.09 us): 30x -> ~2.4x, and 2.4x is
INSIDE the engine gap (faster-codegen-suggestions.md section 8: cl-ppcre
~3.7x behind perl's engine) -- the remaining lever on this shape is the
PCRE2 sb-alien FFI future item, not more PCL plumbing.  Curve stays linear.
After-fix profile: ppcre engine ~25%, set-match-vars+%p-at-elem-set ~18%,
do-regex-match glue ~8%, clear ~6% -- broad, no single lever left.

PROBES vs perl 5.40.3, all byte-identical: the 7-row capture-lifetime
probe (0-group clears / fail keeps / fewer-group excess / %+ / $^N / @-
sizes), the 4-row @-/@+ aliasing probe (\$-[0] and \@- across matches --
was DIVERGENT before), and an 18-row wide probe (split, s///, s///e /g,
scalar+list /g, named captures, \G loop, interpolated /$pat/g, qr identity
==, qr match, tr, /abc/ vs /abc/i memo separation, high-water across group
counts, pos(), a .= -built subject, s///r).  Guards: Pl/t/match-vars-01.t
31 -> 34 rows (magic-element aliasing, per-perl clearing across group
counts, memo keying).  tools/bench-exec.pl gained a `regexg` row so later
rounds track this shape.

RESIDUE FILED AS #770: the s/// twin -- `$n++ while $x =~ s/a/b/` emits
(p-subst "a" "b") per ITERATION and do-regex-subst re-runs
perl-regex-to-ppcre + the scanner format key per execution; same memo
treatment applies (p-subst-op is mutated nowhere; watch the replacement
lambda identity).  Not taken here: #680 is the m// family.
subject: Target-A residue: a scalar-context m//g match costs ~2.6 us in PCL vs ~0.09 us in perl -- LINEAR now (#477) but 30x off; profile the per-match allocations (@-/@+ rebuild, clear-capture-groups' 20 writes, the scanner cache key)
